the taxonomic status and phylogenetic relationship of the seven species of Capillariidae, which are of medical importance to humans and animals.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
molecular data, especially the 18S-rDNA sequence, can complement morphological characters in the taxonomic identification of capillariids, particularly when species are morphologically similar.
the seven capillariid species isolated here are genetically distinct and that the molecular phylogeny based on the 18S-rDNA sequences is consistent with the morphological taxonomy.
the 18S ribotype of E. perforans is distinct from that of E. contortrus, and that the two Capillaria species in this study, i.e., C. phasiani and C. pudendotecta, are distinct species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
molecular phylogeny based on the 18S-rDNA gene sequence is useful for species identification of capillariids, and that it can be used to supplement morphological data.
molecular genetic data are useful for the identification and phylogenetic relationships of species of capillarids in poultry.

morphological and molecular-genetic approaches are useful for identifying species of capillarid nematodes in birds, and that molecular-genetic analyses are essential in the case of morphologically similar species.
